hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $112^\circ$ and $38^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 112^\circ - 38^\circ = 30^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is one hundred twelve degrees. Angle B is thirty-eight degrees. Angle C is thirty degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $DEF$ has angle measures of $38^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180 ^\circ- 38^\circ - 30^\circ = 112^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle DEF$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle D E F. Angle D is one hundred twelve degrees. Angle F is thirty degrees. Angle E is thirty-eight degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $HIG$ has angle measures of $94^\circ$ and $38^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 94 ^\circ- 38^\circ = 48^\circ$.  



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle HIG$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle G H I. Angle G is ninety-four degrees. Angle I is thirty-eight degrees. Angle H is forty-eight degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, only $\triangle DEF$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.
